paper: Khosla, Ratan Murty and Kanwisher 2022, Current Biology
title: Replaying the food response in visual cortex

steps.title: Brain responses to photographs
steps.paper: The authors recorded fMRI responses while people viewed a large set of complex photographs.
steps.here: The app has no scanner. Isaac renders paired scenes and TRIBE predicts the brain's response to each one.

steps.title: Decomposing without a hypothesis
steps.paper: They split the voxel responses into their main components using a data-driven method that started from no hypothesis.
steps.here: The app does not run that decomposition. It reads named brain regions instead, so it can only test a category someone has already chosen.

steps.title: Known categories come back
steps.paper: The method recovered components already known to respond to faces, places, bodies and words, which served as a check on it.
steps.here: The app checks its own pipeline the same way, with a finished study comparing faces against vases of the same size.

steps.title: A food component appears
steps.paper: They found an unexpected component that responded selectively to images of food and had its own anatomical layout.
steps.here: The app reads one ventral region for food against objects of the same shape. Food was chosen in advance here, not discovered.

steps.title: Could colour explain it?
steps.paper: They tested whether low- and mid-level features such as colour, shape and texture could account for the food component's responses.
steps.here: This step previews the colour-matched study in greyscale, so Isaac re-renders it and TRIBE reads it again. It is only a preview and the finished study is not re-run.

steps.title: Matched-stimulus control run
steps.paper: They ran high-throughput tests and control experiments with matched stimuli, using a computational model of the component.
steps.here: This step copies the colour-matched study, switches it to greyscale and runs a few pairs. TRIBE plays the part of the computational model.

bindings.b: an object of the same colour

steps.title: Registered, then replicated
steps.paper: They registered their methods and hypotheses before testing, then repeated the findings in held-out participants and in a new dataset.
steps.here: The app has no new people or new datasets. As a weaker stand-in, it re-runs the shape-matched pairs from a camera angle the study never used.

args.title: Food against shape-matched objects, new camera

bindings.b: an object of the same shape
